name: 42656-mixedprompt-32b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1)
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process vLLM engine (guidellm `vllm_python`), no router, no external cache tier.
architecture: dense decoder, Qwen2ForCausalLM, 64 layers, 40 query heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 5120, vocab 152064, 32.76B parameters in bf16
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=10, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 6000 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, static seed 42656.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, temperature 0, bimodal by construction. 10% of requests carry one of 36 fixed 896-token prefixes; 90% carry one of 60 fixed 64-token prefixes (73 tokens each). Every request adds a 9-token unique body and generates exactly 30 tokens. Prefixes are drawn independently per request, so long and short interleave at random. At block-size 128 a long request's shared prefix is exactly 7 KV pages and a whole short request is one partial page, so the recurring content is 36 x 7 = 252 pages against the 300-page pool and a given long prefix comes back about every 360 requests.
purpose: A 32-billion-parameter assistant giving short fixed-length answers to ten concurrent users, mixing brief and long shared-template prompts on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. Engine: source checkout of
# 9d4dc4ca2fefae1a19648d7989f1dffb351e1b29 (`git describe --tags`: v0.23.1rc0-86-g9d4dc4ca2fef).

model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-32B
tensor-parallel-size: 1
enable-prefix-caching: true
max-model-len: 30000
max-num-seqs: 50

# NOT the engine default: at 0.90 the KV pool on this card is smaller than this workload's
# recurring prompt content, so the pool is pinned rather than left to the default.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.95

# NOT the engine default (16). The KV page is the unit this workload's recurring prompt
# content is measured in: a 896-token long prefix is exactly 7 pages and a 116-token short
# request is one partial page, which is what makes the pool arithmetic below exact rather
# than an estimate off a memory profile.
block-size: 128

# The pool is pinned to a block count instead of being whatever the memory profile leaves
# over, because the whole operating point is the ratio between the pool and the recurring
# prompt content: 36 long prefixes x 7 pages = 252 pages of recurring content against 300
# pages of pool, i.e. the content occupies 84% of the pool and the run is a reuse-under-
# pressure measurement rather than reuse into an empty cache. 300 x 128 x 256 KiB = 9.4 GiB,
# which fits inside what `gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` leaves after 61.0 GiB of bf16 weights.
num-gpu-blocks-override: 300

# Deliberately absent: dtype/quantization (the checkpoint declares bf16), enforce-eager
# (CUDA graphs stay on), max-num-batched-tokens, --host/--port (the engine is driven
# in-process).
